messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired — PD-INC-3456 — severity: P1. Trigger: redis-maxclients spike in prod-us-east-1 cluster. Auto-notify to eng-oncall.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty event created: https://pd.example/PD-INC-3456 — escalation policy: db-oncall -> eng-sre. First responder: sara.

sara: acked on PD and taking. seeing lots of `maxclients` errors from the proxy pool. metrics: redis clients jumping from ~800 -> 5400 over 30s.

matt: @sara are these coming from a single service / route? any customer reports?

sara: preliminary traces show a ramp from inbound inference traffic to the routing gateway (api-gw). suspect a bursty client. no confirmed customer impact yet but some 503s from request router.

alex: throwing up redis `INFO clients` from one node: ```# Clients
connected_clients: 5302
blocked_clients: 120
``` hitting `maxclients` (default 10000?) but pgbouncer/proxy limits are capping at 5k which is tripping.

jin: quick mitigation: can we rate-limit at the API gateway or squash retries? I can patch the gateway to 429 for noisy IPs.

ops-bot: Runbook suggestion: 1) isolate noisy sources via ACL, 2) drain workers for suspect service, 3) increase redis accept queue / worker pool or add read replica.

sara: doing step 1 now — adding a temporary route block for the top 10 offending IPs (observed from logs). command: ```kubectl -n infra exec deploy/api-gateway -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/ban -d '{"ips": ["10.8.12.4","13.52.2.11"]}'```

matt: putting canary limits in place on gateway too, config snippet: ```rate_limit: 
  enabled: true
  requests_per_minute: 1200
```

sara: pushed the gateway patch, rolling restart in progress. watching redis metrics.

(ops-bot reacts :thumbsup: to sara)

alex: after the gateway patch, connected_clients dropped to ~1300 over 45s. blocked_clients slowly went down. but p50 latency for redis SET increased from 3ms -> 18ms during the spike.

jin: good. next: increase pgbouncer pool connections for the app tier to reduce queuing. will bump from 2000 -> 3500. doing in 1m.

sara: also scaling down a noisy batch worker deployment that was retrying a failed loop. `kubectl scale deploy/noisy-batch --replicas=0` executed. logs show repeated reconnect loops to redis.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-3456: acknowledged by sara at 1781234565. Escalation timers paused.

alex: load is stabilizing, connections down to ~900, 503s dropped to normal. still seeing a small error spike from retries. recommend keep mitigations for 30m and monitor.

matt: any customer-facing impact? support slack shows one customer report (acct: paywise) saw a transient 502s at 03:12 UTC. I'm drafting a short note.

sara: marking customer impact: transient 5xx for a small subset of API calls — likely <0.1% of requests during 03:11-03:16 UTC.

jin: will open a follow-up GH issue for long-term: "retry-guardrails and gateway backoff". suggested owners: platform/gateway + infra/db.

ops-bot: Suggested post-incident actions: add better client-side backoff guidance, instrument per-route connection counts, and add automatic throttling on per-customer burst above threshold.

alex: we should also consider increasing redis sentinel maxclients on the short-term staging cluster to test.

sara: agreed. for now I'm releasing the noisy ACLs and scaling the batch service back up to 2 replicas slowly to verify no repeat.

matt: handoff to morning oncall (alex) at 04:00 UTC. leaving PD on for 60m.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-3456: status updated -> monitoring. assigned to: alex.

alex: will monitor for next hour, follow-up doc in #incidents with timeline + graphs. thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident closed (auto) at 1781234620 after monitoring window. Summary: transient redis connection saturation driven by noisy batch retries; mitigations: gateway rate-limits, ACL bans, scale adjustments. Postmortem task created: https://go/ops/PD-3456-postmortem
